claims.text: Short-range-order percolation in HfNbTaTiZr forms ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The ordered binary clusters reduce local lattice-distortion amplitude relative to a random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS to higher frequencies.
Reduced lattice distortion lowers high-frequency phonon-scattering rates.
Chemical ordering consequently produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant local lattice distortion and broad high-frequency phonon-DOS features caused by mass variance and strain-field scattering.
Monte Carlo-induced SRO can yield percolating HfTi and TiZr clusters and transient or stable B2-like structures.
The range 300–1200 K permits SRO evolution without melting in HfNbTaTiZr.
The ordered clusters form distortion-relief zones with lower RMS atomic displacement than the random matrix.
The ordered clusters maintain a continuous percolative network for phonon transport.
Transition from random to ordered binary phases reduces local chemical-potential variance and lattice strain fields.
A percolating SRO network produces phonon channeling that overrides scattering from ordered-phase boundaries.
In FeNiCrCoCu, increasing temperature from 300 K to 600 K reduced dislocation density and increased elastic modulus from 173 GPa to 219 GPa.
The FeNiCrCoCu dislocation-recovery result is analogous to ordering-induced reduction of phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
The SRO-percolated state will show sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS peaks and a lower Debye-Waller factor than the random state.
Below the SRO-cluster percolation threshold, HfNbTaTiZr retains the low conductivity of a random alloy, whereas above it the ordered network dominates transport.
Above an order-disorder transition potentially exceeding 1200 K, B2-like ordering dissolves and conductivity returns to the random-alloy baseline.
PMC11355469 shows that disorder increases with temperature.
